page: Hetzner Cloud ccx43 is a dedicated CPU server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 62.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 360 GB NVMe SSD, and the virtualized environment operates under a QEMU hypervisor without any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth (62.67 GB/sec read and 48.85 GB/sec write for large blocks), and software compilation speeds fall within the average range. The instance demonstrates average performance for database operations, processing 20.97 million Redis SET operations per second, and static web serving at 14.54 GB/sec. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with 70B model prompt processing scoring in the bottom 10%, though text generation on smaller 135M models remains strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ccx43 offers a balanced resource density profile, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources with a proportional memory allocation and local NVMe storage without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. This makes it highly suitable for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, medium-scale database operations, and web serving.
